IS : 2961 - 1973

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR CHROME RETAN FINISHED UPPER LEATHER

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 J a n u a r y 1973, after the draft finalized by the Leather Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This s t a n d a r d was originally published in 1964. In this revision, values for solvent extractable substance, chromium content, hide substance, tensile strength and elongation have been modified. Requirements for grain strength has been omitted and flexural endurance ( bally ) test has been introduced. A list of recommended fungicidal additives has also been included for guidance of the manufacturers. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a standard is complied with, the final value, ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be IS : 2-1960*. T h e number of significant off value should be the same as that of the 1. S C O P E 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for chrome retan finished leather for footwear uppers involving only partial retannage. 1.1.1 This standard covers only such leathers as are partially or completely tanned with basic chromium salts initially, followed by retannage, including mordanting with vegetable or synthetic tanning materials or in combination with both of these materials. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard the definitions given in IS : 1640-1960 shall apply.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). Glossary of terms relating to hides, skins and leather.

particular requirement of this observed or calculated, expressrounded off in accordance with places retained in the rounded specified value in this standard.

3

IS : 2961 - 1973 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 R a w M a t e r i a l -- T h e material shall be cattle hides cured by wet salting, brining, drying or dry salting. 3.2 T a n n i n g -- T h e material shall be tanned first with basic chromium salts, followed by retanning with suitable vegetable or synthetic tanning materials or a combination of these. 3.3 F i n i s h i n g -- T h e tanned leathers shall be fat-liquored and oiled, if necessary. After dyeing, or as such, and after correction of the grain, if necessary, it shall be finished suitably. T h e grain shall be tight and shall be well set out to make it smooth and even. T h e leather shall be free from cuts and open surface blemishes. 3.4 F u n g i c i d a l A d d i t i v e s -- At the end of the tanning operation and before drying, suitable fungicides shall be incorporated in the leather in required proportions. Fungicides used to promote mildew resistance in leather shall be effective and non-toxic. T h e leather shall show no growth of mildew when examined visually after the completion of test prescribed in LB : 2 of IS : 6191-197l*. 3.4.1 T h e use of 0.1 percent of fungicidal additives on dry weight basis of the leather is recommended. T h e following fungicides are also recommended as suitable: a)  -chloro- m -cresol; b)  -nitrophenol; c) Sodium penta chlorophenate; d) Sodium trichlorophenate; e) -naphthol; f) o -, m-,  -cresol; and g) Sodium silicofluoride. 3.5 P h y s i c a l R e q u i r e m e n t s -- T h e material physical requirements given in T a b l e 1. shall comply with the

3.6 C h e m i c a l R e q u i r e m e n t s -- T h e finished leather shall also comply with the chemical requirements given in T a b l e 2. 3.7 Size a n d S h a p e -- T h e leather shall be supplied in the form of full pieces or sides, trimmed free of toggle punch and nail marks. 4. M A R K I N G 4.1 T h e area of the leather shall be marked legibly in square decimetres on individual pieces at the tail end of the flesh side. *Methods of micro-biological, colour fastness and microscopical tests for leather.

5. PACKING 5.1 The leather shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 5.1.1 The leather shall be so packed that it shall during transit and in storage be protected against moisture, exposure to direct sunlight and mechanical damage. 6. MARKING 6.1 The packages shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer or recognised trade-mark, if any; type; number of pieces of leather; total area, weight; and month, and year of the manufacture. 5
